II22A-01.note: Key pits quiet+salt (Calder) against noisy+no-salt (Ellery). A and D support the noise hypothesis; B (Brenlow vs Ashby) is confounded and the most tempting since it 'tests' the claim without isolating noise.

II22A-02.note: Cassel vs Fairlie isolates fungi with sun held constant. D (Ardel > Cassel) is tempting because Ardel is the canonical fungus plot, but it varies shade only and supports Ebbert; B also supports shade.

II22A-03.note: Bypass (unlit, traffic) beating lit lanes (lit, quiet) weakens lamps. B is confounded (downtown differs on both factors) and most tempting; A and C support Fairweather.

II22A-04.note: Requires a subtraction plus a threshold across three cells. C (R-8) is most tempting: passes the temperature condition by the widest margin but fails salt (70); A passes salt but fails the 10-minute gap.

II22A-05.note: Carrow Point 35/64 is the only ratio above one-half; Avelin Bar 44/90 (just under half) is the tempting near-miss. Fallow Strand 15/40 is visibly under half.

II22A-06.note: Bramley (2,200 m) at 6.0 is below Carrick (1,800 m) at 6.4; options omit elevations so the student must cross-reference. D is tempting because it names Bramley but compares it to a lower site it exceeds; B and C restate the general trend.

II22B-01.note: North cliff in July (rain, no freeze-thaw) beating its own March (freeze-thaw, no rain) weakens Grieg. A, B, D all support freeze-thaw; a test-wise student may notice the key is the only option where a summer month 'wins'.

II22B-02.note: Sealed wool (lining gas only) beating ventilated cotton (city air only) pits the two sources against each other. D (ventilated wool > sealed wool) is tempting because it mentions wool twice but supports Hult; C is incoherent (sealed cotton has no source).

II22B-03.note: Iselund eruptions rose from 2000-03 (pre-pump, normal rain) to 2005-08 (pumping, normal rain), contradicting Lark. C is tempting (same shape on Kalvnesby) but Kalvnesby is unaffected by pumping, so it says nothing about Lark; B is drought-confounded; A supports Lark. Student must track drought years against 2004.

II22B-04.note: All four options are true and show Hesk losing more; only B uses Garvik, the deepest lake (64 m). Strong 'accurate but beside the point' distractors; identical first clauses mean the student must find the depth column.

II22B-05.note: Ivarsby is the only young-sediment well deeper than 100 m and it exceeds 10. B (Haldor, 130 m, 27) is most tempting: deep and over the limit but old sediment. Options omit depth/sediment, forcing a table lookup; D is under the limit on sight.

II22B-06.note: Joskar (51 km, 22 cm) thicker than Ilvikmoen (38 km, 14 cm) is the only inversion. Distractors are trend-consistent comparisons; a student must check distances since options omit them. Lighter combining than real hard items.

II22C-01.note: Nolvaston (breakfast, tardiness unchanged) vs Rossmere isolates breakfast. A (Mendrick vs Rossmere) is the most tempting but confounded; C and D support Okafor.

II22C-02.note: Pruett (radio, no contact) over Nantle (contact, no radio) weakens Paredes. A is confounded (Mossbury has both) and tempting; B and C support Paredes. Four-town 2x2 requires holding two attributes per town.

II22C-03.note: Fourth floor is the only lottery floor with real daylight. D (third floor) is most tempting since it is a lottery floor, but its windows admit little light; C has daylight but seniority confound.

II22C-04.note: Nuskirk 7/30 (23%) is the only fall above one-fifth. A (Orvel, largest absolute drop of 11) is the tempting distractor; the others sit at 17-18%, close enough to require computation.

II22C-05.note: Medlow is the only market under 50% card acceptance with over 40 shoppers per vendor (45). Options omit the card column, so Nevin (46/vendor) and Rushmere (42) are tempting until the student checks acceptance; Ossiter has <50% cards but only 35/vendor.

II22C-06.note: Quist (70 mi, 66) below Pirrock (57 mi, 72) is the only inversion. D names Quist but compares it with a nearer, cheaper town; A and C follow the trend. Structurally identical to II22A-06 and II22B-06.

II22D-01.note: Wrennick (rain-fed, no fees) vs Skarra (spring-fed, no fees) isolates climate. B (Thrane vs Skarra) is confounded and the most tempting; A supports Sorensen; D runs against Thorvald.

II22D-02.note: Ulving (pine, damp stone) over Tamm (oak, dry timber) weakens the oak hypothesis. C (Selander vs Vass) is confounded and tempting; B and D support Wennberg.

II22D-03.note: Same decade (1740s), river town vs hill town isolates glass access with pattern books held constant. B is tempting (river 1740s vs hill 1710s) but confounded by the 1720 pattern books; A supports Tamsen.

II22D-04.note: Tarrow 60/96 (0.625) is the only ratio under two-thirds; every other mill is exactly 0.70 (Sorrel 0.707). Yarrel's largest absolute drop is the tempting distractor; the identical 0.70 ratios are a mild tell once one is computed.

II22D-05.note: 1500s-1510s is the only steady-paper interval in which book prices fell. B is the strong distractor (paper steady 1480s-1490s but books rose slightly); A and C show falls where paper also fell. Table column lacks units; options supply 'grams of silver'.

II22D-06.note: Sollen: 1.45 s and 8.5 m3/seat. B (Teverin, 7.5) and D (Wrayne, 7.5) pass reverberation and require division to reject; C fails reverberation on sight.
